question: Will Berkshire Hathaway increase its holdings of Alphabet stock in its Q3 2026 13F filing?

calls.reasoning: Threshold equals the exact June 30 holding (78,791,167 A + 27,188,433 C); the $10B June private placement is already in it, so Yes requires fresh Q3 buying. Berkshire's Q3 10-Q shows gross equity purchases of only $2.4B against $2.8B of sales (net seller), with cash going to $9.6B of buybacks. Alphabet has been added every quarter since initiation and is Abel's conviction position, so some of the $2.4B could plausibly be Alphabet, but the small total and net selling make a flat position at least as likely. Filing not yet on EDGAR as of Nov 13; expected Nov 16. No prediction market found.

- The June 2026 private placement ($5B Class A at $351.81 and $5B Class C at $348.20, part of Alphabet's ~$80-85B raise) closed in Q2 and is already in the June 30 count (CNBC 2026-06-01; Yahoo preview).
- Berkshire's Q3 2026 10-Q (filed ~2026-11-07): equity purchases ~$2.4B, sales ~$2.8B, so a net seller; share buybacks ~$9.6B (Kingswell; CNBC 2026-11-07). Which names were bought is not disclosed.
- At ~$350/share, $2.4B would buy ~6.9M Alphabet shares if all of it went there; any amount above 0 shares qualifies for Yes.
- The Alphabet position has been added in every quarter since initiation in late 2025 (Class A held 4 quarters, Class C 2 quarters). Buffett said he initiated the position (CNBC 2026-07-15).
- Alphabet in Q3: capex of $51.4B exceeded operating cash flow (negative FCF); the stock fell about 18% in the month to mid-Nov and is down ~8% YTD (Motley Fool 2026-11-12).
- Status quo / No: the share count is unchanged or lower. Any net sale, even a tiny one, resolves No.
- Resolves off the Berkshire 13F-HR for the period ending 2026-09-30, summed across all classes and entries, not off the 10-Q or press reports. As of 2026-11-13 EDGAR shows no Q3 filing; latest is 2026-08-14. Expected filing Monday 2026-11-16 (45-day deadline falls on Saturday Nov 14).

calls.reasoning: Threshold equals the exact June 30 holding, so Yes needs any net Q3 addition. Q3 equity purchases were only ~$2.4B against $2.8B of sales. But the 'commercial, industrial and other' category, which Alphabet falls in, rose ~$2.3B at cost net of sales, so nearly all buying went into Alphabet's bucket. Alphabet is a conviction position added in 3 of 4 quarters since initiation. Against that, other names in the bucket compete for the money, and a hold after the big Q2 build is a common pattern. The price drop came after 9/30 and doesn't matter. No human market found.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the facts: threshold equals the Q2 holding, the placement is already in the Q2 count, the 10-Q shows $2.4B bought vs $2.8B sold, and the filing is pending. The runs differed mainly in weighting. Run 2's point that the commercial/industrial/other category, which includes Alphabet, gained ~$2.3B at cost net of sales means Q3 buying was concentrated in Alphabet's bucket rather than spread thin. That is stronger Yes evidence than the 'net seller' framing suggests. Competing names in the same bucket (energy, possibly homebuilders) and a typical post-build hold keep it below even. I could not verify the category classification on this run (no web access); I relied on Run 2's dossier. No market found; nothing retrieved by me.
